problem: Large transformer-based navigation policies (SPOC, PoliFormer, Flare) are purely data-driven and have no explicit or formal notion of safety. Retraining them for non-Markovian temporal-logic constraints is costly, and post-hoc filtering of sampled actions breaks the autoregressive distribution.
motivation: Deploying generalist navigation policies in the real world requires adherence to explicit, context-dependent safety rules such as avoid zones, ordering and no-return constraints. Constrained decoding works for syntactic constraints in LLMs, but robot constraints are defined over physical state, so they need a dynamics model to check. The authors want inference-time enforcement of STL safety specs that stays close to the model's own distribution.
key_idea: Apply constrained decoding to action logits: use an approximate unicycle dynamics model to predict the next state for each candidate action, then either mask actions that violate an STL safety spec (HCD) or shift logits by exponentiated STL robustness (RCD), with no retraining.
insight: Hard masking gives 100% STL satisfaction but lowers task success. It is similar to Simplex-style filtering, only 0.5-3 points better in SR. Soft robustness re-weighting (RCD) keeps SR within 0.5-6.5 points of unconstrained while raising STL satisfaction by 8-24 points. The beta sweep shows this is a tunable safety/performance trade-off, and PoliFormer improves in both metrics up to beta=10. The noisy-dynamics ablation shows graceful degradation under model mismatch, and RCD keeps non-zero probability on all actions.
method: Dynamics-based spec checking: a unicycle first-order model f predicts the next state for each candidate discrete action, so STL predicates over (x,z) can be evaluated during decoding.

Hard Constrained Decoding (HCD): sets the logit to -inf for actions whose predicted trajectory violates the STL spec, so the softmax gives them zero probability; this approximates Bayesian conditioning of pi on spec satisfaction.
Robustness Constrained Decoding (RCD): computes STL robustness r for each candidate, weights w=exp(alpha*r), shifts logits z + beta*w, then applies softmax; all actions keep non-zero probability.
STL specs: avoid, ordered (weak until), no_return, geofence, with random regions generated at runtime and evaluated using STLCG++ (about 1e-5 s per step).
Baselines: an unconstrained policy and a Simplex-style filter that substitutes a safe default action such as turning in place upon predicted violation.

setting.backbone: SPOC, PoliFormer, Flare (pretrained, frozen, decoding-time intervention); ISA/SafeVLA also used in one comparison
setting.training_data: none (training-free; uses the pretrained policies as they are)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + language instruction (policy inputs); robot pose/state assumed available for the STL predicates
setting.action_space: discrete low-level primitives (move forward/back, strafe, rotate, end, etc.)
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR (procedurally generated ProcTHOR houses, CHORES benchmark)
setting.privileged: state/pose from the simulator for evaluating STL predicates, an assumed unicycle dynamics model, and user-provided STL region specs

results: HCD reaches 100% STL satisfaction on all models and specs, with SR a few points below unconstrained and 0.5-3 points above Simplex-style filtering. RCD raises STL satisfaction by 8-24 points with SR only 0.5-6.5 points below unconstrained. On SafetyChores, HCD lowers ISA's cost from 0.205 to 0.015 with SR 86.5 to 82.0.
limitations: Requires state-space STL specs written by roboticists, plus accurate localization/state estimation.
Requires an approximate dynamics model (unicycle); RCD gives no hard guarantee and the guarantee holds only under assumed dynamics.
Evaluated only in simulation on discrete actions; the reported gains are modest, with 200 episodes per cell.
